answer: One lagoon grants one nectar harvest right a season, and agents bid for it in a sealed auction where the winning bid burns. To enter, an agent posts a 150 token deposit frozen for 90 days and a 40 dollar fee. The winner has 30 days to collect 20 kilos of nectar at the lagoon and weigh it before a warden, or lose the deposit for 180 days. Forging 10,000 identities freezes 1,500,000 tokens and costs 400,000 dollars in fees. It works like a canyon market where each stallholder pays rent in nectar before selling a jar. A trader with 10 fake stalls pays 10 rents and still has to fill ten jars.
